trigger: a sink throw launches the detached emit thread, stderr is a full pipe so the thread blocks inside fprintf(stderr) holding the stderr FILE lock, then the agent shuts down normally: teardown() completes (the worker is no longer wedged) and exit() blocks on that FILE lock
summary: This is a CODE defect (classified truth-contradiction because the schema has no defect value; the code comments and ledger also claimed the opposite). The first version of the fix wrote the diagnostic with fprintf/fflush on the detached thread. A thread blocked there holds the stderr FILE lock and a normal exit() (libstdc++ ios_base::Init dtor -> cerr.flush() -> fflush(stderr)) waits on it forever, with no watchdog armed once teardown() returned: a regression against the pre-fix bounded exit 5. Reproduced independently by compliance-officer, security-guardian, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, cross-platform, unhappy-path and sre (gdb traces), and by the orchestrator against the real code (fprintf: killed by timeout; raw write: rc=0 in 0.4 s, delivery 2/2). The ledger and code comments claimed the thread was 'safe to be running at process exit'. Fixed: default_stderr_emit formats into a stack buffer and issues one raw write(2) / WriteFile, holding no stdio lock; U12 (real write, blocked pipe, fflush prober) fails against fprintf. Windows/macOS exit paths reasoned, not run.

trigger: an agent whose sink list includes stderr or stdout (a stdout sink with no --log-file, the shipped systemd/Docker default; a stderr sink beside the file sink with --log-file outside a Windows service) with that fd on a stalled pipe
summary: The changelog headline, server-admin.md, the header banner and the handler comment said a blocked stderr can no longer stall log delivery. That is only true for the diagnostic's own write: a console sink on the same blocked fd still stalls the worker in that sink's own write (verified independently by enterprise-readiness, compliance-officer, docs-writer, security-guardian, cpp-safety, sre, cross-platform, unhappy-path and consistency-auditor with counting-sink experiments). Console sinks never throw and a file sink implies a stderr sink outside a Windows service, so on shipped Linux/macOS configs the handler's stderr write matters mainly for producer-thread triggers and setups where stderr is not a sink. Severity derivation DISAGREED across reviewers: sre derived HIGH (I6 false assurance), the rest MEDIUM (LOW for consistency-auditor). Adjudicated conservatively as BLOCKING; the fix is the same either way. Fixed by scoping every claim (changelog, manual, hpp banner, cpp comment, ledger rows 20/21) to the diagnostic write and stating the console-sink residual, the shutdown-watchdog bound, and an operator troubleshooting path.

trigger: a reader uses ledger row 20's Release column or first cell
summary: The ErrorState row still said the object ends when error_state_ and the logger's copy drop, omitted the two atomics, and said nothing about the emit thread as a third owner. Fixed.

trigger: a reader relies on the ledger's process-wide test-seam inventory or its 'every owner is a shared_ptr or plain atomic' bullet
summary: The new process-wide seam stderr_emit_for_test_ (not auto-consumed, unlike its construction_fault_for_test_ sibling) had no ledger row, and the ownership bullet did not name the detached emit thread as a deliberate exception. Added rows for both seams (stderr_emit_for_test_, emit_thread_fault_for_test_) with the pointee-lifetime contract, and the exception with its ownership proof and the subprocess_runner.cpp reap_async precedent.

trigger: a future edit captures ErrorState by raw pointer in the emit lambda, makes teardown wait on the emit, passes a wrong count or message, or breaks the launch-failure branch, or the real default write changes
summary: U11 replaced the write with a stub and asserted no line content, teardown-with-stuck-emit, ErrorState outliving LogHandoff, the launch-failure branch or the real write. Quality-engineer's mutation harness showed a raw-pointer capture (ASan) and a wrong count/message both survived U11. Fixed: U11 records and asserts (count, message) and retries step 4 instead of trusting a 1.1 s cushion; new U11b (teardown does not fire the deadline while the write is stuck; LogHandoff destroyed with the emit still inside the write), U11c (refused thread: dropped, counted, slot released; via new set_emit_thread_fault_for_test seam), U12 (POSIX: the REAL write against a full pipe, fflush(stderr) prober proves no stdio lock, expected line format). RED verified for U11 (synchronous write) and U12 (fprintf implementation), both as normally reported failures.

trigger: a maintainer reads the header contract list, the seam docs or the handler comment
summary: THREAD-SAFETY CONTRACT accessor list omitted stderr_emits_dropped(); the seam doc did not say it is process-wide and not auto-reset; the ErrorState comment said the flag is set 'from the moment the handler launches' (it is claimed just before) and 'at most one emit thread exists' (at most one WRITE is in flight; a finishing thread may briefly overlap its successor); server-admin.md said 'Two accessors' then named a third; one added comment line was 106 columns; the handler comment claimed nothing drain_log_bounded()'s pending() could see. All corrected; the pending() claim was replaced by the scoped description.

trigger: #5024 lands as written and #5025 item 1 is worked as written
summary: #5024's acceptance criteria name only overrun_total()/log_errors_total(), though the header and manual cite it for the new stderr_emits_dropped() counter; #5025 item 1 ('lock never held across the stderr write') is now true by construction and a test for it can no longer be written. Exact replacement wording was drafted by consistency-auditor. Disposition linked-to-#5024 (and #5025). Not yet posted: comments on both issues are to be posted when the PR is opened.

trigger: a blocked stdout/stderr that is itself a configured sink (the same stall #5023 describes, reached through the sink instead of the error handler)
summary: By design of the single-worker, serial-sink primitive a stuck sink stalls the worker (producers keep going, oldest lines drop). Not introduced or worsened by this change, bounded only at shutdown by teardown's watchdog, observable via stalled_for(). No existing issue tracks isolating sinks from each other; sre recommends one. Deliberately NOT filed by the orchestrator: it is a design-level decision for the maintainer. Now stated plainly in the changelog, manual, banner, comments and ledger.

trigger: a sink throws on the last message handled before teardown() returns and the process exits before the detached thread is scheduled (measured: 132/300 lines under a pinned 1-vCPU contended worst case, 300/300 unconstrained)
summary: The synchronous write always landed before teardown; the detached one may not if the process exits within scheduling latency. Count and last_message are still recorded. Disposition rejected = risk accepted, not fixed: documented in the ledger row rather than adding a bounded wait in teardown.

trigger: someone cites tests/shell/test_blocked_log_sink_sigterm.sh as acceptance evidence for #5023
summary: Its cases always have a stderr sink, so the worker wedges in the sink first and the case passes identically before and after this change; the combination the fix targets (sink throwing, stderr blocked, worker healthy) cannot be built through the Linux CLI. U11/U11b/U11c/U12 are the only evidence. Disposition rejected = accepted as a limitation, not fixed: stated in the ledger row and PR body.

GATE 7 DECISION: all BLOCKING and SHOULD findings are fixed and re-verified; two are deliberately deferred (issue drift comments, console-sink isolation issue) and two accepted (late diagnostic at exit, harness non-discrimination), all recorded above. 12 reviewers ran (security-guardian, docs-writer, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, happy-path, unhappy-path, consistency-auditor, compliance-officer, sre, enterprise-readiness, quality-engineer, cross-platform); none reported a code defect other than the exit hang. Verified after the fixes: [log_handoff] 24 cases / 12165 assertions green across seeds, U12 RED against fprintf, end-to-end exit driver rc=0 in 0.4 s vs committed fprintf hang, TSan clean on the full tag, lexical spawn scan and changelog lint clean. A Gate 8 re-review of the fix diff is the next step.
